messages:
maya: Heads-up — after yesterday's kernel/quant change I see a spike in perceived streaming latency for small interactive requests. p95 went from 120ms -> 230ms, p99 ~ 540ms -> 1.2s. Noticed delta tied to token streaming flush interval and microbatch sizing. Anyone else seeing this?

sam: yep saw alerts. Looks correlated with the new kernel selector that favors fewer kernel-switches (good for throughput) but that bumped the stream-flush default to 30ms.

jon: tl;dr: larger flush interval = fewer syscalls and better throughput, but users perceive lag on first tokens. For chat UX we care about time-to-first-chunk more than aggregate throughput.

priya: telemetry I pulled — breakdown for 1k requests sampled:
```
before: time-to-first-byte p95=115ms, p99=420ms, overall tokens/s 120k
after:  p95=230ms, p99=1200ms, overall tokens/s 160k
```
Seems throughput improved ~33% but TTFB doubled for tail.

leo: KV cache note: with larger flush windows we keep KV in-flight longer and drop fewer microbatches, but when we flush at chunk boundaries we trigger more KV spills for long contexts. That increases variance for certain clients.

maya: important: this regression surfaced in the hosted default; Dedicated customers hitting strict latency SLOs flagged it. We need options: 1) revert flush default 2) make flush adaptive (latency tier + typing signal) 3) expose microbatch target per-route.

sam: quick experiment — lowered flush interval to 8ms in a canary for small chat routes, everything else same. Results: p95=125ms, p99=480ms, tokens/s ~148k. So small throughput hit but big perceived latency win.

jon: suggests an adaptive heuristic: if request is streaming and expected token rate < X, set flush=8ms, else use 30ms. Also consider a "first-chunk immediate" path: always emit first N tokens as soon as available.

priya: profiling showed kernel switch cost isn't the main culprit. The cost appears at the flush serialization layer: lock contention and wakeups for tiny batches when flush interval fires. Attaching snippet of perf flame (abridged):
```
0.12 wake_up_hrtimer
0.10 flush_worker (locks)
0.08 kv_cache::serialize
0.06 kernel_dispatch
```
So we can optimize flush path or adjust interval.

leo: FYI kv cache behavior: when we make more frequent flushes, we increase KV hits because prefetched prefixes get reused, but we also increase contention on the cache lock (observed). Two knobs: per-shard locks + lockless read or coarse-grain batching.

maya: action items I propose:
- canary adaptive flush heuristic on chat routes (sam)
- microbatch target per-route toggle in config (enable for Dedicated) (jon)
- short-term: revert global default to 12ms to buy time (may)
- infra perf ticket to look at flush path locks (priya)

sam: infra-bot: start canary for "adaptive-flush-chat" on 5% of traffic for region us-west-2

infra-bot: Canary started: adaptive-flush-chat @ 5% (us-west-2). Canary id=cf-20260304-09. Will report metrics in ~15m. :rocket:

jon: sample config I'm testing:
```
streaming:
  flush_interval_ms: 30    # default
  adaptive:
    enabled: true
    first_chunk_force_emit: true
    small_stream_ms: 8
    threshold_token_rate: 20  # tokens/sec
```
Switchable via route metadata.

priya: perf ticket created: PERF-4372 "flush_worker lock hotpath" with profile attached. Adding backlog items for lockless read and per-shard KV locks.

leo: note for rollout: Dedicated customers often pin the server config; exposing microbatch/flush per-route is safer than changing default.

maya: +1. Also we should add p95/time-to-first-chunk to the console default dashboard for streaming routes so product can track UX regressions.

sam: canary preliminary after 20m: adaptive flush reduced time-to-first-chunk p95 from 230ms -> 130ms, tokens/s drop ~7% on that route. No CPU saturation observed.

maya: perfect. I think we ship adaptive flush for interactive routes and leave bulk endpoints on throughput-optimized defaults. Document the tradeoffs in the release note.

jon: also adding a fallback: if latency SLO missed, auto-decrease flush interval for that route for next N minutes. Simple policy: step-flush -50% on SLO miss, cooldown 5m.

priya: re: KV cache, I'll prototype lockless read in a spike branch and measure. Expect small latency gains for high-concurrency small streams.

leo: will prepare customer-facing note for Dedicated customers about per-route knobs.

maya: thanks team. I'll file the release note draft and assign follow-ups. :thumbsup:

sam: quick reminder — add an e2e test that simulates typing (sparse token stream) vs bulk generation so we don't regress again.

maya: agreed. Closing thread after follow-ups.
